name: Amaimon
confidence_why: The only description of Amaimon, the three-page SIL phonology data sheet checked by Lillie (2001), says stress does not seem to be phonemic and never states where it falls, and neither Z'graggen (1975) nor Pick (2020) says anything about stress, so the record rests on one uncontradicted first-hand source.

catalog_locator: OPD section 'Suprasegmentals (tone, stress, length)', p. 2 (the only stress statement in the document)

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote confirmed verbatim in the OPD text we hold at the stated place; it is the document's only suprasegmental sentence and no example carries stress marks, so not determinable (non-phonemic stress asserted, position never stated) is the faithful code. (2) The deciding source is a 3-page unreviewed SIL workshop data sheet (2001) — minimal, but every catalogue I could open (Glottolog 5.1 bib: 3 Z'graggen survey items, 0 descriptive refs; SIL archive: 1 item; OLAC 2025: OPD + audio deposits only) and Pick 2020 p. 203 ('available data.. very limited', citing only Lillie 2001) show it is the only written phonological statement on Amaimon. Z'graggen 1971 (held) explicitly omits stress for the whole Madang survey; Z'graggen 1975 PL C-38 (downloaded now, p. 584) and 1980 PL D-31 (held) are silent.
